02 · Product Types

Three faces, one core.

Every Lentopan® board shares the same EPS-granule lightweight concrete core. What differs is what's already on the surface when it arrives.

Sade Lentopan®

Plain, both faces

Uncoated on both sides. The base board for sites applying render, tiling, or their own cladding system directly.

Tek Yüzey Alçıpan

Plasterboard, one face

9 mm plasterboard factory-bonded to one side — ready for taping, skim and paint with no secondary lining.

Tek Yüzey Fiber-Cement

Fibre-cement, one face

6 mm or 8 mm fibre-cement bonded to one side, for exposed, wet-area or fire-line finishes.

03 · Description

Why teams switch to it.

The board itself

  • All-in-one insulation, acoustic and A1 fire-rated core
  • Vapour-permeable — dries out rather than trapping moisture
  • Doesn't promote mould, even if wet before the building is watertight
  • Suitable for pre-build, Cat A and Cat B fit-outs
  • Standard 60 × 120 cm sheet, 3–20 cm thickness on request
  • MEP routing pre-formed off-site or cut on-site to suit

Why it's fitted this way

  • Joints bonded with a light bead of PU foam, fixed with trapezoidal screws
  • Any direct finish follows — render, plasterboard, fibre-cement
  • Fewer wall build-ups and components to manage on site
  • Fewer site visits, simpler project sequencing
  • Single-material board recycles fully at end of service life
  • A sustainable alternative to brick, aircrete block and similar systems

Finishes applied directly to the board

07 · Fixing Details

How a wall goes together.

Four parts, repeated across every opening.

1

Lentopan® board

60 × 120 cm, set into the light-gauge frame.

2

Light steel frame

Carries and aligns each board within the wall run.

3

PU foam

A light bead behind each board bonds it to its neighbour.

4

Fixing screw

Trapezoidal screws set boards to the frame, max. 600 mm apart.

08 · FAQ

Before you specify.

What sizes does Lentopan® come in?

A standard 60 × 120 cm sheet, produced in thicknesses from 3 cm to 20 cm depending on the insulation and fire performance the wall needs.

Can it get wet on site before the building is watertight?

Yes. Lentopan® is vapour-permeable, isn't damaged by water, and doesn't encourage mould growth — so it can be installed ahead of the building envelope being closed up.

What finishes can go directly onto the board?

Render (with a mesh coat, painted or bare), plasterboard, fibre-cement, and ceramic tiling have all been applied directly to the board face.

How is it fixed together on site?

Boards sit in a light steel frame, bonded to each other with a light bead of PU foam at the joints and fixed to the frame with trapezoidal screws, spaced no more than 600 mm apart.

How much labour time does it actually save?

Time-and-motion case studies referenced in the technical catalogue show install labour reduced by more than 65% compared with a conventional block-and-render or stud-and-board build-up.

What happens to it at end of life?

It's a single-material, all-in-one board, so waste on site is minimal and offcuts are recyclable. At the end of its service life the board itself can be recycled back into new production with zero waste.

Can services be routed through it?

Yes — mechanical, electrical and plumbing routes can be pre-formed off-site to a project's design, or cut into the board on site.
